title: Price every rebuilt child and keep accepted material separate from correct sequence
statement: For IID attempts at a fusion node with accepted probability q_v=p_v+f_v>0, destruction/rebuilding of both children on every rejection and cost c_v per attempt, the expected consumed resource is C_v=(C_left+C_right+c_v)/q_v. For constant q,zero overhead,L=2^k, expected C_L=(2/q)^k; q<1 gives unbounded retry support, not a finite worst-case budget. Correct accepted-junction purity is(p/q)^(L-1) only with correct leaves and independent local junction errors. Polynomial material cost is not verified-correct yield or elapsed time.

requires: IID per-node accepted attempts independent of child history/resources; rejected attempts destroy both submitted children; explicit leaf/join costs.
Constant-size-independent q for the polynomial law; local junction error independence and correct leaves for the purity product; boundary q/c unchanged by subprotocol for the stated DP.

assumptions: Material per accepted product is not material per verified-correct product, throughput or practical advantage.
Size-law n must be defined; the written exponent2 uses total output length, not child length.
costs: Count all rebuilt leaves, lost children, connectors, join operations, purification, wash/time and final validation; no free oracle for correctness.
contract.units: C counts declared material/resource units; p,f,q dimensionless per attempt; kappa inverse declared size.
contract.obstruction: Measure whole-node acceptance, false acceptance and size dependence with a real junction-sensitive protocol.

body: C is an expectation. At q<1 any finite retry count can be exceeded with positive probability; no hard material/time bound follows. Renewal gives C=A+(1-q)C with A including both child costs and join overhead on every attempt. Interpret p as correct new-junction acceptance, not a promise that previously wrong children become correct. A persistent wrong bond passing the same connectivity test is not removed by repeated identical washing. Boundary-only q_i,c_i independent of chosen child sizes/protocol give C(i,j)=min_k[C(i,k)+C(k+1,j)+c_k]/q_k, O(L^3) time/O(L^2) storage; size-dependent protocols require additional state. The acquired size_dependent_cost code uses n=2,4,...,L as TOTAL NEW PRODUCT length in q(n)=q0*exp(-kappa*n). Thus C_L=L*q0^(-log2 L)*exp(2*kappa*(L-1)). If n instead denotes each child length, the multiplier is exp(kappa*(L-1)). Retain the convention; neither is a measured steric law. Obtaining a verified-correct product additionally requires an actual discriminating reader and its full costs.

review.scope: Completed source-exposed intake-author reconstruction of covalent graph connectivity versus identity; renewal rebuild and independent accepted-junction purity, explicit total-product-size steric exponent and boundary-independent optimal-tree substructure; odd-fragment endpoint parity and exhaustive four-port counterconstruction; stationary two-click hazard law; independent exponential-clock Laplace/Jensen and conditional-deadline argument. The entire acquired1023-word library was independently checked over522753 unordered pairs: distinct length10 ACGT strings, min aligned Hamming3, GC4-6 and no homopolymer triple. Small exact rational checks verify model recurrence/parity/port/DP scope without executing original research programs. Correct-pair success versus acceptance and total-product versus child length are explicit qualifications, not silently blended. Three original programs were fully read, not run; missing import, numerical simulations, primary chemistry papers, measured performance, novelty and practical advantage are outside acceptance.
